text:
tara: trying to run `redwoodctl init demo --local` on a corp Win image and it fails during the initial login with a permission error. localserve never starts. anyone hit this?

ben: what does the terminal show?

tara: small paste:
```
> redwoodctl init demo --local
device code flow started, open https://redwood.auth/ and enter code X1Y2-Z3W4
waiting for auth...
error: failed to open profile: permission denied
failed to start localserve: open C:\Users\tara\AppData\Local\Redwood\profiles.json: access denied
```

alex: corp AV sometimes locks AppData
 -> quick check: try running an elevated shell to confirm it's a perms thing
 -> or set REDWOODCTL_HOME to a user folder you control and retry

ben: example workaround (powershell):
```
setx REDWOODCTL_HOME "%USERPROFILE%\.redwood"
# restart shell
redwoodctl login --headless --profile=tara-dev
redwoodctl init demo --profile=tara-dev --local
```

tara: setx trick let login finish but then localserve failed with "bind: address already in use". turned out an old test process held 3000. killed it and init succeeded.

alex: good catch. two docs actions: note AppData vs LocalAppData perms in Windows quickstart, and add a troubleshooting blurb for port conflicts with `redwoodctl localserve ps` and `--port 0`.

ci-bot: Created ticket DX-5120: "redwoodctl: Windows AppData permissions + REDWOODCTL_HOME workaround; mention localserve port conflicts"

tara: posting steps here so others don't waste time. thanks! :coffee:
